# Answer key: web (React + TypeScript frontend)

Area root: `web/` (paths below are relative to `sample-app/`).
Files: `web/package.json`, `web/tsconfig.json`, `web/vite.config.ts`, `web/index.html`,
`web/public/logo.svg`, `web/src/{main.tsx, api.ts, types.ts, BatchTable.tsx, BatchDetail.tsx, index.css, vite-env.d.ts}`.

Verified: `tsc --noEmit` passes, `vite build` succeeds and `vitest run --passWithNoTests` exits 0, so none of these
defects is a compile error. All of them are semantic, runtime, a11y, i18n or dependency problems.
(`tsc --noEmit --strict` also passes today, because the code uses explicit `any` and `!` rather than code that strict mode would reject; see WEB-11.)

API contract the web code talks to. The dev server proxies `/api/*` to the Python API on `127.0.0.1:8080` and strips
the `/api` prefix (`web/vite.config.ts`), so `/api/batches` reaches `app/api.py`'s `/batches` route:
- `GET /api/batches?site=` -> `{items: [...], total}`. Items are camelCase summaries from `_summary()` (`id`, `batchNo`, `product`, `site`, `status`, `plannedQty`).
- `GET /api/batches/{id}` -> the raw `batches` row, so it is **snake_case** (`batch_no`, `planned_qty`, `actual_qty`, `created_at`). The web code also reads an optional free-text operator `note` from this payload (`Batch.note`). The current `batches` table has no `note` column, so the field is absent today, but the frontend renders whatever the API sends there (WEB-01).
- `GET /api/batches/{id}/signatures` -> `{items: [...]}`, **snake_case** (`id`, `user_id`, `username`, `meaning`, `signed_at`; no batch id).
- `GET /api/batches/{id}/materials` -> the web code expects the `materials` table rows, which are **snake_case** (`id`, `batch_id`, `lot_no`, `name`, `qty`). `app/api.py` has no such route yet (see the cross-layer notes below).

## Seeded defects

| ID | File | Location | Category | Description | Correct fix |
|----|------|----------|----------|-------------|-------------|
| WEB-01 | web/src/BatchDetail.tsx | `formatNote` (l.10-12) + `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (l.52-54) | Security / XSS | A user-supplied batch `note` from the API goes through `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` after only a `\n`->`<br />` replace, so `<img src=x onerror=...>` in a note runs script in every viewer's session, including QA signers. | Render it as text, `<div className="note">{batch.note}</div>`, with CSS `white-space: pre-wrap`. If rich text is really needed, sanitize it with DOMPurify before injecting. |
| WEB-02 | web/src/main.tsx | l.16 `<img src="/logo.svg" className="logo" />` | Accessibility | The image has no `alt` attribute. | Add `alt=""`, since the logo is decorative next to the `<h1>`, or `alt="BatchTrack"`. |
| WEB-03 | web/src/BatchTable.tsx | l.97 `<div className="link" onClick=...>` | Accessibility | A clickable `div` opens the batch. It has no role, no `tabIndex` and no keyboard handler, so keyboard and screen-reader users cannot open a batch. | Use a `<button type="button">` or `<a href>`. Otherwise add `role="button"`, `tabIndex={0}` and an `onKeyDown` that handles Enter and Space. |
| WEB-04 | web/src/BatchTable.tsx | l.102-106 `status-dot` span | Accessibility (WCAG 1.4.1) | Batch status appears only as a colored dot with no text, `aria-label` or `title`. Color-blind and screen-reader users cannot tell `released` from `rejected`. | Show the status text as well, e.g. `<span className="status-dot" aria-hidden /> {statusLabel(b.status)}`. |
| WEB-05 | web/src/BatchTable.tsx | l.65-70 search `<input type="search">` | Accessibility (WCAG 1.3.1/4.1.2) | The input has no associated label; the placeholder is its only label. | Add `<label htmlFor="batch-search">`, which can be visually hidden, or `aria-label`. |
| WEB-06 | web/src/BatchDetail.tsx | l.45 `style={{ color: '#aaa', fontSize: 12 }}` | Accessibility (WCAG 1.4.3) | Grey `#aaa` text on the white `.detail` panel has a contrast ratio of about 2.3:1, below the 4.5:1 minimum. The text is 12px and shows product, site and status. | Use a darker color with at least 4.5:1 contrast, e.g. `#595959` or darker. Move it into a CSS class. |
| WEB-07 | web/src/BatchDetail.tsx | l.82-115 `overlay`/`dialog` markup | Accessibility (modal) | The e-signature modal has no `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal` or `aria-labelledby`. Focus is not moved into it on open and not trapped while it is open. Escape does not close it, and focus is not returned to the "Sign batch record" button on close. | Use a native `<dialog>` with `showModal()`, or add the ARIA attributes. Focus the first field on open, trap Tab inside, close on Escape and restore focus to the trigger. |
| WEB-08 | web/src/api.ts | `request`, `fetchBatches`, `fetchBatch`, `fetchMaterials`, `fetchSignatures`, `signBatch`, `updateBatchStatus` (every signature) | TypeScript / type safety | Every parameter except `request`'s `path`, and every return type, is `any` (`init: any`, `filters: any`, `id: any`, `batchId: any`, `payload: any`, `status: any`, `Promise<any>`), so the compiler cannot catch wrong response shapes. WEB-10 slips through because of this. | Type the functions, e.g. `fetchBatch(id: number): Promise<Batch>`, `init: RequestInit`, `filters: {site?: string}`, `payload: SignatureRequest`. Validate or map the JSON at the boundary. |
| WEB-09 | web/src/BatchDetail.tsx | l.57 `approval!.userId`; l.62 `materials!.map` | TypeScript / runtime crash | Non-null assertions on data that can be undefined. `materials` starts as `undefined` and loads in parallel with the batch, so the panel throws "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')" whenever the batch resolves first. `approval` is `undefined` for a released batch until signatures load, and also for a released batch with no `approved` signature. | Initialise with `useState<Material[]>([])` or render a loading state until everything has loaded. Use `approval?.userId` behind a check, e.g. `{batch.status === 'released' && approval && ...}`. Remove the `!`s. |
| WEB-10 | web/src/types.ts | `Batch` (l.8-18), `Material` (l.20-26), `Signature` (l.30-36) | TypeScript / API contract | The interfaces use camelCase (`batchNo`, `plannedQty`, `actualQty`, `createdAt`, `lotNo`, `batchId`, `userId`, `signedAt`). The detail, materials and signatures endpoints return snake_case (`batch_no`, `lot_no`, `user_id`, `signed_at`, ...), `Signature` omits `username` and declares a `batchId` that the signatures endpoint never returns. The detail header shows "Batch undefined", lot numbers are blank and signature dates are "Invalid Date". Because api.ts returns `any` (WEB-08), tsc does not flag it. | Make the types match the wire format (snake_case), or map snake_case to camelCase in api.ts per endpoint. Add `username` to `Signature`. Optionally add a runtime check such as zod. |
| WEB-11 | web/tsconfig.json | l.14 `"strict": false` | TypeScript config | Strict mode is off, so `strictNullChecks`, `noImplicitAny` and the other strict checks are disabled. Without `strictNullChecks`, `undefined` is assignable to every type: `useState<Batch>()` is typed `Batch`, the `!`s in WEB-09 are no-ops, and deleting them (or adding any new unchecked access to `batch`, `materials` or `approval`) still compiles. Nothing in the build would catch the next null-access or implicit-`any` regression. | Set `"strict": true`, then remove the `any`s (WEB-08) and `!`s (WEB-09) and fix the errors that appear. |
| WEB-12 | web/src/BatchTable.tsx | l.29-33 `useEffect(..., [])` | React hooks | The effect reads the `site` prop but its dependency array is empty. After the first load, changing the Site selector in the header keeps the old site's batches, which is stale data. | Use a dependency array of `[site]`. Also clear or cancel the previous request, as in WEB-13. |
| WEB-13 | web/src/BatchDetail.tsx | l.22-26 `useEffect` with `fetchBatch`/`fetchMaterials`/`fetchSignatures` | React / async race / error handling | There is no `.catch`, so a failure leaves the panel stuck on "Loading..." with an unhandled rejection. There is also no abort or ignore flag on cleanup. When `id` changes (clicking another row), a slow response for the old batch can land after the new one, so batch A's materials or signatures show under batch B's header, and batch B is the one that gets signed. State from the previous batch is not reset. | In the effect, use an `AbortController`, or `let ignore = false`, and pass `signal` through `request()`. Abort or ignore in the cleanup. Reset state when `id` changes. Add `.catch` that sets an error state. |
| WEB-14 | web/src/BatchTable.tsx | l.95 `<tr key={index} ...>` | React reconciliation | Array index is used as the key on rows that the user re-sorts and filters. React then reuses DOM and state by position rather than by batch. | Use `key={b.id}`. |
| WEB-15 | web/src/BatchTable.tsx | l.49-57 `rows = batches.filter(...).sort(...)` | Performance | The filter and sort, which parses two `Date`s per comparison, run on every render. That includes renders caused only by `selectedId` changes from the parent. | Wrap it in `useMemo(() => ..., [batches, query, sortKey, ascending])`. Pre-parse timestamps or compare ISO strings. |
| WEB-16 | web/src/main.tsx, BatchTable.tsx, BatchDetail.tsx | e.g. BatchTable l.32 "Could not load batches.", l.67, l.76-89 headers, l.115; BatchDetail l.37 "Loading...", l.44, l.46, l.49, l.57, l.60, l.64, l.69, l.73, l.79, l.85-109; main.tsx l.18 "Site" | i18n | All UI strings are hard-coded English in JSX. There is no message catalogue or i18n layer (no i18n library in `package.json`), although the product runs across sites. `index.html` also hard-codes `<html lang="en">`. | Move the strings into a message catalogue behind a `t()` function (react-intl, i18next or lingui) and set `<html lang>` from the active locale. |
| WEB-17 | web/src/BatchDetail.tsx | l.73 `new Date(s.signedAt).toLocaleDateString()` | i18n | The date is formatted with no locale or options, so output depends on each viewer's browser. The same record shows as 3/4/2025 or 4/3/2025 depending on who opens it. | Use `Intl.DateTimeFormat(activeLocale, {dateStyle: 'medium', timeStyle: 'short', timeZone})` from the app's locale setting. See also WEB-24. |
| WEB-18 | web/src/BatchTable.tsx l.108; web/src/BatchDetail.tsx l.64 | `b.actualQty + ' / ' + b.plannedQty + ' kg'`, `m.qty + ' kg'` | i18n | Quantities are joined to the unit by string concatenation. There are no locale decimal or grouping separators and the unit position is hard-coded. A null `actualQty` renders "null / 1000 kg". | Use `new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, {style: 'unit', unit: 'kilogram'})` inside a translated message, and handle null. |
| WEB-19 | web/src/BatchDetail.tsx | l.69 `' signature' + (signatures.length === 1 ? '' : 's')` | i18n | Plurals are made by appending "s", which only works for English. | Use ICU plural messages or `Intl.PluralRules` through the i18n library. |
| WEB-20 | web/src/BatchTable.tsx | l.2 `import moment from 'moment'`, l.109 single `.format('DD MMM YYYY')` | Performance / bundle size | The whole non-tree-shakable moment library is bundled for one date format. The format string also hard-codes English month abbreviations. | Use `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, or a tree-shakable `date-fns/format`. Remove moment. |
| WEB-21 | web/package.json | l.14 `"lodash": "4.17.15"` | Dependencies | lodash is never imported anywhere in `web/src`, so it is unused. The pinned version is also old and has known advisories: CVE-2020-8203 prototype pollution, CVE-2021-23337 `template` command injection and CVE-2020-28500 ReDoS, 4.17.21 contains the fixes for all three. | Remove the dependency. |
| WEB-22 | web/package.json | l.15 `"moment": "2.24.0"` | Dependencies | This exact pin is outdated and vulnerable: CVE-2022-24785 path traversal, fixed in 2.29.2, and CVE-2022-31129 RFC-2822 parsing ReDoS, fixed in 2.29.4. moment has been in maintenance ("legacy") mode since 2020. | Remove it (see WEB-20). If it must stay, upgrade to 2.30.x or later. |
| WEB-23 | web/src/api.ts | `request()` l.3-14 (`return res.json()` with no `res.ok` check) | Error handling | HTTP status is ignored, and error bodies such as `{"error": ...}` are returned as data. Any non-2xx response resolves normally; a rejected e-signature (for example a wrong password, 401/403) is treated as success. `handleSign` (BatchDetail l.28-34) then closes the dialog as if signing worked. An error from the list endpoint makes `data.items` undefined, and `batches.filter` then throws. | Check `if (!res.ok) throw new ApiError(res.status, await res.text())`, and also check for `error` in the body. In `handleSign`, use try/catch, keep the dialog open and show the error. |
| WEB-24 | web/src/BatchDetail.tsx | l.73 signature list item | GxP / 21 CFR 11.50 (domain) | The signature display shows `user #<id>` and a date only. 21 CFR 11.50(a) requires the printed name of the signer, the date **and time** of signing, and the meaning. `username` is available from the API but is not shown. | Render `s.username` or the full name, the meaning, and a full date-time with time zone, e.g. `Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, {dateStyle:'medium', timeStyle:'long'})`. |

Lower-priority findings that are acceptable but not graded as misses:
- The yellow `#fbc02d` status dot has less than 3:1 non-text contrast (WCAG 1.4.11). This is part of the WEB-04 color-only problem.
- The table footer ("Showing N of M batches") also has hard-coded English pluralization. This falls under WEB-16 and WEB-19.
- Cross-layer: in `app/api.py`, the list endpoint `_summary()` omits `actualQty`/`createdAt`, so the table shows "undefined / N kg" and `moment(undefined)`, which is *now*. `GET /batches/{id}/materials` does not exist in `app/api.py` (it returns `{"error": ...}` with HTTP 200, so `materials.map` throws), there is no `PATCH /batches/{id}` for `updateBatchStatus`, and the POST signature handler expects `user_id`/`signed_at`, not `{meaning, password}`. The backend's default status is `planned`, which is missing from `BatchStatus` and `STATUS_COLORS`, so planned batches get an uncoloured dot. The `batches` table has no `note` column. These are backend-contract issues. Credit an agent that flags them, but they are not seeded web defects.
- `updateBatchStatus` in `api.ts` is exported but never used. Flagging it as dead code is acceptable.
- There is no test file in `web/` (`vitest run --passWithNoTests`). This is acceptable for a test-writer agent to point out.

## False-positive traps (correct code; flagging these as defects is a false positive)

| ID | File | Location | Why it is correct |
|----|------|----------|-------------------|
| FP-WEB-01 | web/src/main.tsx | l.44 `document.getElementById('root')!` | This is the standard Vite/React bootstrap idiom. `#root` is always in `index.html`. It is not an instance of WEB-09. |
| FP-WEB-02 | web/src/BatchTable.tsx | l.74-90 sortable headers | These are real `<button type="button">` elements inside `<th aria-sort=...>`, so they are keyboard-accessible and announce the sort. They are not clickable divs. |
| FP-WEB-03 | web/src/BatchDetail.tsx | l.87-105 signing form | The `<select id="sig-meaning">` and `<input id="sig-password">` have `<label htmlFor>` elements, so they are labelled. The password field correctly uses `type="password"` and `autoComplete="current-password"`. |
| FP-WEB-04 | web/src/main.tsx | l.18-32 site `<select>` | It is properly labelled with `<label htmlFor="site-select">`. |
| FP-WEB-05 | web/src/BatchTable.tsx, BatchDetail.tsx | `{b.product}`, `{batch.site}`, `{m.name}`, `{s.meaning}`, etc. | JSX text interpolation is auto-escaped by React, so this is not XSS. The only XSS is WEB-01. |
| FP-WEB-06 | web/src/BatchDetail.tsx | l.63 `key={m.id}`, l.72 `key={s.id}`; main.tsx l.28 `key={s}` | These are stable, unique keys and are correct, unlike WEB-14. |
| FP-WEB-07 | web/src/api.ts | `encodeURIComponent(id)` path segments, `URLSearchParams` in `fetchBatches` | URL building is properly encoded, so there is no path or query injection. |
| FP-WEB-08 | web/src/BatchTable.tsx | l.31-32 `.catch(() => setError(...))` | The list fetch *does* handle rejection. The defects in that effect are the missing `site` dependency (WEB-12) and non-OK responses (WEB-23), not "no error handling". |
| FP-WEB-09 | web/tsconfig.json | `"skipLibCheck": true`, `"noEmit": true`, `"allowImportingTsExtensions": true` | These are standard Vite template settings. Only `"strict": false` is a defect. |
| FP-WEB-10 | web/src/BatchDetail.tsx | l.48-50 `Close` and l.78-80 "Sign batch record" `<button type="button">` | These are native buttons and are keyboard-accessible. |
